roles.label: Vendor
roles.duty: Owns the label. Must disclose what the score predicts, subgroup calibration on need as well as cost, and known limitations, and must fix the model when a deployer's audit fails.

roles.label: Hospital AI governance
roles.duty: The accountable party for deployment. Commissions the AIA, approves or blocks go-live, sets re-assessment triggers and answers to patients and regulators for the outcome.

roles.label: Hospital data science
roles.duty: Runs the local label-validity and disparity tests (G1–G2), sets thresholds against capacity, and builds the monitoring dashboard.

roles.label: Clinicians / care managers
roles.duty: Make the final enrolment decision, can override the score with recorded reasons, and report suspected misses. Their decisions are audited by group too.

roles.label: Equity / ethics officer
roles.duty: Independent check on G1–G3, runs the patient panel, and handles complaints from people who were ranked.

roles.label: Payer
roles.duty: Where the payer licenses or mandates the tool, it shares responsibility for its effects (Section 1557 reaches covered health programmes).

roles.label: Patients / community
roles.duty: Are told an algorithm is used, are consulted on the AIA, and can contest a referral decision.

roles.label: Regulator
roles.duty: Sets the binding floor: what must be assessed, disclosed and monitored, and enforces it.

actions: State the training label in the first line of documentation, not the appendix.
Report calibration on need (conditions, biomarkers) by race, sex and age, alongside calibration on cost.
Offer a health-weighted or blended-label version, as the vendor did after 2019.
Run gates G0–G6 before go-live and on every new version or threshold.
Name one accountable executive and publish the assessment summary.
Collect race and ethnicity data for auditing, under strict purpose limitation.
Treat the score as a referral aid, not an eligibility test; record override reasons.
Audit enrolment decisions by group quarterly, alongside the score itself.
Extend 45 CFR 92.210(b) to tools whose labels, not only inputs, can encode protected-trait disparities.
Restore an effects-based route for proxy discrimination in federally funded health programmes.
Clarify that private hospitals rationing access to care fall under Annex III 5(a) or a FRIA-equivalent duty.
Use the new Art 4a bias-detection basis to require, not just permit, subgroup testing.
Turn ICMR's validity and fairness principles into binding pre-deployment checks for hospital AI.
Designate large health data fiduciaries as Significant Data Fiduciaries so Rule 13 algorithm checks apply.
